title: Trust region and cubic regularization methods

items.title: Quadratic trust-region models and the actual-to-predicted reduction ratio
items.statement: Define the quadratic model m(p)=f(x)+gᵀp+½pᵀBp on the Euclidean ball ||p||₂≤Δ, its predicted and actual reductions, and their ratio when predicted reduction is positive.

items.title: The cubic-regularized quadratic model
The natural logarithm is bounded above by its positive argument minus one
items.statement: For every real x>=1, prove 0<=log x<=x-1<=x.

items.title: Global trust-region minimizers satisfy the shifted-Hessian conditions, including the hard case
items.statement:
Let $n\ge1$, let $B\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ be symmetric, let $g\in\mathbb R^n$, and
let $\Delta>0$. Every global minimizer $p_*$ of
$$q(p):=\langle g,p\rangle+\tfrac12p^TBp\quad\text{over }\|p\|_2\le\Delta$$
has a multiplier $\lambda\ge0$ such that
$$(B+\lambda I)p_*=-g,\qquad B+\lambda I\succeq0,\qquad \lambda(\Delta-\|p_*\|_2)=0.$$
Conversely, every feasible $p_*$ satisfying these conditions is a global
minimizer. A global minimizer always exists.

The singular hard case is included as follows. Let $\mu$ be the least
eigenvalue of $B$ and $E_\mu$ its eigenspace. If $\mu<0$, $g\perp E_\mu$,
and the solution $p_0$ of
$(B-\mu I)p_0=-g$, $p_0\perp E_\mu$, has $\|p_0\|_2\le\Delta$, then
$$p_*=p_0+z,\qquad z\in E_\mu,\qquad \|z\|_2^2=\Delta^2-\|p_0\|_2^2$$
is a global minimizer with the singular multiplier $\lambda=-\mu$. If
$\|p_0\|_2<\Delta$, both signs of any chosen nonzero $z$ of the required
length give distinct minimizers.

items.title: A finite-budget trust-region method with ratio-based radius updates
The actual-to-predicted ratio approaches one at small radii away from stationarity
items.statement:
Let $m$ be the model of
[[def-trust-region-quadratic-model-and-ratio]], with $g\ne0$, symmetric
$B$, and radius $\Delta>0$. Suppose $\|B\|_2\le M_B$ for a declared
$M_B\ge0$, and $f$ is $C^1$ on an open set containing the segment from $x$
to $x+p$. Suppose the gradient of $f$ is $L$-Lipschitz on that segment,
meaning
$$\|\nabla f(u)-\nabla f(v)\|_2\le L\|u-v\|_2$$
there. Let $0<\theta\le1$, let $p$ be feasible, and suppose
$$m(0)-m(p)\ge\theta\,[m(0)-m(p_C)]$$
for the Cauchy step $p_C$ of [[alg-trust-region-cauchy-step]]. Interpret
$\|g\|_2/(2M_B)=+\infty$ if $M_B=0$, and assume
$\Delta\le\|g\|_2/(2M_B)$. Then the predicted reduction is positive and
$$|\rho(p)-1|\le\frac{2(L+M_B)\Delta}{\theta\|g\|_2}.$$
Consequently, for $0<\eta_2<1$, if $L+M_B>0$ and
$$\Delta\le\frac{\theta(1-\eta_2)\|g\|_2}{2(L+M_B)},$$
then $\rho(p)\ge\eta_2$. If $L+M_B=0$, then $\rho(p)=1$.

items.title: Cubic regularization bounds consecutive unsuccessful trials
items.statement: Under the stated regularization floor and cap, exact-Hessian Lipschitz model, and multiplicative rejection update, bound rejected trials per successful trial by an explicit constant independent of ε.

items.title: Cauchy-decrease trust-region iterations have liminf gradient norm zero
items.statement:
Let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ be $C^1$, bounded below, and have an
$L$-Lipschitz gradient on every trial segment. At every iteration let $B_k$
be symmetric with $\|B_k\|_2\le M_B$ for a fixed $M_B\ge0$. Fix
$0<\eta_1<\eta_2<1$, $0<\gamma_{dec}<1<\gamma_{inc}$, $0<\theta_C\le1$,
and $0<\Delta_0\le\Delta_{max}$. Start from any $x_0\in\mathbb R^n$ and
consider an infinite-horizon trajectory that at each nonstationary iteration
follows the model-formation, step-selection, ratio, and radius-update rules of
[[alg-trust-region-method]], with target $0$ and its finite outer-cap return
omitted. If this trajectory is infinite, then
$$\liminf_{k\to\infty}\|\nabla f(x_k)\|_2=0.$$

items.title: Trust-region first-order complexity counts both successful and unsuccessful trials
items.statement:
For every nonstationary trial of [[alg-trust-region-method]], the selected
predicted reduction is positive, and every accepted trial strictly decreases
the objective.

Assume the hypotheses and parameter ranges of
[[thm-trust-region-global-liminf-gradient]], and let $f_{inf}$ be a lower
bound for $f$. For each target $0<\varepsilon\le1$, consider the
infinite-horizon trajectory that follows the nonterminal transition rules of
[[alg-trust-region-method]] with target $\varepsilon$, omitting its finite
outer-cap return, until its first iterate with
$\|\nabla f(x_k)\|_2\le\varepsilon$. Define
$$c_\delta:=\min\left\{\frac1{2M_B}, \frac{\theta_C(1-\eta_2)}{2(L+M_B)}\right\},\qquad c_R:=\min\{\Delta_0,\gamma_{dec}\min\{c_\delta,\Delta_{max}\}\},$$
where a zero denominator means $+\infty$, and put
$$c_P:=\min\{c_R,1/M_B\},\qquad c_S:=\tfrac12\eta_1\theta_Cc_P>0.$$
Then the number $N_s$ of accepted steps before reaching the target and the
number $N_u$ of rejected trials obey
$$N_s\le\frac{f(x_0)-f_{inf}}{c_S\varepsilon^2},$$
$$N_u\le\frac{\log(\Delta_0/r_\varepsilon)+N_s\log\gamma_{inc}} {|\log\gamma_{dec}|},\qquad r_\varepsilon:=\min\{\Delta_0,\gamma_{dec}\min\{c_\delta\varepsilon, \Delta_{max}\}\}.$$
Here $\log$ denotes the natural logarithm of a positive real.
Consequently, accepted steps and total trials $N_s+N_u$ are
$O(\varepsilon^{-2})$ as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$. An outer cap at least
the resulting total-trial bound suffices for the finite-budget algorithm to
return `target-achieved` or `stationary`, with gradient norm at most
$\varepsilon$.

items.title: Adaptive cubic regularization reaches first-order accuracy in O(ε⁻³ᐟ²) evaluations
items.statement:
Let $n\ge1$, and let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ be $C^2$ and bounded
below by $f_{inf}$.
Run [[alg-adaptive-cubic-regularization]] with exact Hessians and parameters
$0<\eta_1<\eta_2<1$, $\gamma_{up}>1$, $0<\gamma_{down}<1$,
$0<\kappa<1$, $0<\kappa_\theta<1$, and
$0<\sigma_{min}\le\sigma_k\le\sigma_{max}$ with $\sigma_{max}\ge3L$.
Suppose the Hessian is $L$-Lipschitz on every trial segment, and let
$0<\varepsilon\le1$. Let $R\in\mathbb N_0$ satisfy
$\gamma_{up}^R\sigma_{min}\ge3L$ (take $R=0$ if
$\sigma_{min}\ge3L$).

For the counts below, use the trajectory that follows the trial,
acceptance/rejection, and regularization-update rules of
[[alg-adaptive-cubic-regularization]] with its finite outer-cap return
omitted. The finite-cap conclusion then reinstates that return.

The algorithm has two complexity guarantees.

1. **Exact model minimizers.** If every solver call returns an exact global
   minimizer, define
   $$C_g:=\sigma_{max}+\sqrt n\,L,\qquad c_g:=\frac{\eta_1\sigma_{min}}{6C_g^{3/2}}.$$
   Through the first iterate with gradient norm at most $\varepsilon$, the
   numbers $N_s$ of accepted steps and $N_u$ of rejected trials satisfy
   $$N_s\le [f(x_0)-f_{inf}]c_g^{-1}\varepsilon^{-3/2}+1,\qquad N_u\le R N_s.$$

2. **Admissible inexact model steps.** Suppose each solver-success candidate
   passes the cubic solution, residual, and Cauchy-decrease checks in
   [[alg-adaptive-cubic-regularization]], and $\nabla f$ is $K$-Lipschitz
   on every trial segment. If the solver succeeds at every nonterminal
   trial, define
   $$D_g:=\frac{\sigma_{max}+\sqrt n\,L+\kappa_\theta K} {1-\kappa_\theta},\qquad c_a:=\frac{\eta_1\sigma_{min}}{6D_g^{3/2}}.$$
   Then the same counts satisfy
   $$N_s\le [f(x_0)-f_{inf}]c_a^{-1}\varepsilon^{-3/2}+1,\qquad N_u\le R N_s.$$

In either case the uncapped process reaches a stationary or target-achieved
iterate with gradient norm at most $\varepsilon$. For the finite-cap
algorithm, an outer cap at least
$$(R+1)\left(\frac{f(x_0)-f_{inf}}{c\,\varepsilon^{3/2}}+1\right)$$
suffices, where $c=c_g$ in case 1 and $c=c_a$ in case 2. The resulting
number of outer trials, and their function, gradient, and Hessian evaluation
counts, are $O(\varepsilon^{-3/2})$. These counts do not bound the internal
work of the model solver.
